transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I came in because I just can't seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. I work as a credit counselor, and lately, I'll sit down and just stare at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list... and I end up rereading the same line over and over again. Then I just put off making the calls entirely. It just feels like even simple decisions are a lot harder than they should be right now.
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty focusing and staying on task since you were a child, or is this a relatively new change for you?

No, it's not something I've dealt with since I was a child. It really started... well, this has been going on since my close friend died. That was a little over two years ago. I never really had this much trouble staying on task before that happened.
Since that loss two years ago, have you also felt persistently sad, empty, or lost interest in the activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. Most days, there's just this... dull heaviness sitting with me. It doesn't really go away. And as for losing interest, well, even when I'm at the community center or out in my garden—places that really used to lift me up—I don't feel much of anything anymore. I just feel like I'm going through the motions with a smile pasted on my face.
During these periods where you feel this heavy, have you ever heard or seen things that others around you did not seem to perceive?
No, I haven't had anything like that happen. I've never seen or heard things that weren't there. It's really just the sadness and the trouble focusing that I've been dealing with.
When you are feeling this heavy, do you find that your movements or speech have slowed down to the point where others might notice, or do you feel restless and unable to sit still?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed my speech or movements slowing down, and no one else has pointed anything like that out to me. And I don't really get restless or fidgety, either. It's really just that heavy feeling on the inside, but physically, I think I'm moving around normally.
During these past two years, have there been times when your symptoms were severe enough that you were unable to function at work or in your daily life for a period of time?

Well, yes, it has affected things. I wouldn't say I've been completely unable to function, but... it definitely gets in the way. At work, at the credit office, I've started postponing my client follow-ups. I just keep pushing them off. And in my personal life, I've really stepped back from things I always used to do. I used to make a point of attending gallery events, and going on outings with my walking club, but... I just don't go to them anymore. I just don't have it in me right now.
Over these past two years, have there been any periods of two months or longer where you felt completely like your old self again, without these feelings of sadness or loss of interest?

No, not really. There hasn't been a time like that. It's just been a constant... heaviness, I guess you could say, for the whole two years. I haven't had a break from it for two months, or even a few weeks, really. It's just always there.
